raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

On system-first chat templates (Qwen, Llama, Mistral), inline `system` messages in the Anthropic `/v1/messages` conversation are merged into the leading system block by `_convert_to_chat_completion_request`. This rewrites the start of the rendered prompt every turn, invalidating the radix prefix cache and forcing a full re-prefill on every request.

The issue reporter measured: prefix cache hit rate **32% -> 96%**, mean TTFT **8.3s -> 0.5s** on a 94K-context agent session after applying this fix.

### Root cause

The conversion loop (lines 411-417 on main) hoists every inline `system` message into `openai_system_content`, which feeds the single leading `system` turn. As the conversation grows, new system instructions mutate the prefix shared by all prior turns, breaking cache matching.

## Modifications

Remove the hoisting loop. Instead, attach each inline system message to the **preceding** user or tool message, wrapped in `<system>...</system>` tags (via a new `_attach_inline_system` helper). If there is no preceding user/tool message (inline system is the first message), it becomes a standalone `user` message.

The top-level `system` field still populates the leading system block, so templates that require a system-first layout remain satisfied. Earlier turns are now immutable across requests, restoring prefix cache stability.

This follows the approach outlined in the issue by @xjdr-alt.

### Files changed

- `serving.py`: removed the inline-system hoisting loop; added `_attach_inline_system()` helper; updated the message conversion loop to call it for inline system messages.
- `test_serving.py`: updated 3 existing tests to assert the new attach-in-place behavior; added 4 new tests covering prefix cache stability, tool-result attachment, leading inline system, and constructed `AnthropicMessage` objects.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable -- this changes message layout only (no kernel or model forward code). Verified via 7 unit tests (3 updated + 4 new) that the converted messages match expected structure.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No direct benchmarks (needs a running model). The issue reporter's measurements on a 94K-context agent session show the expected impact of restored prefix caching: TTFT 8.3s -> 0.5s, cache hit rate 32% -> 96%.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

                 openai_messages.append({"role": "user", "content": list(parts)})
             parts.clear()
 
+        def _attach_inline_system(text: Optional[str]) -> None:
+            """Keep a mid-conversation system message at the position it arrived.
+
+            The chat template cannot render a system role here (that is why
+            this is the merge path), so the text is appended to the preceding
+            user or tool message, or emitted as its own user message when there
+            is none.  Earlier turns then render identically from request to
+            request, preserving the prefix cache.
+            """
+            if not text:
+                return
+            note = f"<system>{text}</system>"
+            prev = openai_messages[-1] if openai_messages else None
+            if prev is not None and prev.get("role") in ("user", "tool"):
+                content = prev.get("content")
+                if isinstance(content, str):
+                    prev["content"] = f"{content}\n\n{note}" if content else note
+                    return
+                if isinstance(content, list):
+                    content.append({"type": "text", "text": note})
+                    return
+            openai_messages.append({"role": "user", "content": note})
+
         # Convert messages
         for msg in anthropic_request.messages:
             if msg.role == "system" and self._merge_inline_system:
+                _attach_inline_system(_extract_system_text(msg.content))
                 continue
             if isinstance(msg.content, str):
                 openai_messages.append({"role": msg.role, "content": msg.content})
